#1725. What Tom Brady's exit means for Birmingham City: Why NFL legend quit St Andrew's, 'body coach' Alex Guerrero's future role revealed - and impact on Knighthead's ambitious £2bn plans for Premier League push and new stadium

Published: 08:41 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 11:15 EST, 10 November 2026

Tom Brady has quit Birmingham but his influence will continue to be felt around the Championship leaders through one of his closest allies.

The club announced via a social media post late on Monday that the NFL legend’s three-year association with Blues would end.

Titled ‘Tom Brady Departure’, the 62-word statement read: ‘Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

'It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.’

Yet it can be revealed that the ideas of Brady’s ‘body coach’ Alex Guerrero will continue to inform Blues’ push for Premier League football.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the reasons for Brady’s departure – and what the future holds for Blues now he has gone...

Tom Brady (right) has left Birmingham City - though their plans remain ambitious under owners Knighthead and chairman Tom Wagner (left)

Brady brought stardust with him to Birmingham and was the figurehead of a new era at the club - despite attending just four matches since buying into Blues

Brady has not been a visible presence in Birmingham for about two years and attended only four matches after he was unveiled as a ‘minority investor’ in 2023, not long after US investors Knighthead had completed their takeover.

It has proved challenging for Brady to divide his time between Birmingham and his commitments in the US, where he has a £280million contract as Fox Sports main NFL analyst. He has also been part-owner of the Las Vegas Raiders since 2024.

Daily Mail Sport understands, however, that Guerrero’s methods will still be used at Blues – a significant detail given his long-term association with Brady.

Described by Brady as his 'body coach', the pair have worked together for two decades and Brady credits Guerrero with extending his NFL career beyond his 45th birthday. With Guerrero at his side, Brady won four Super Bowls and three MVP (Most Valuable Player) awards.

Birmingham chiefs have been very impressed with Guerrero, who they believe has transformed the club’s approach to fitness and recovery.

Since Guerrero came in with Brady, recovery sessions the day after a game have been mandatory and players have had individual conditioning programmes, including tailored advice on nutrition.

Daily Mail Sport understands the methods of Brady's 'body coach' Alex Guerrero (left) will still be used at Blues

In 2025, skipper Christoph Klarer told Daily Mail Sport: ‘We have so many physios and massage therapists who show you exercises in the gym and treat you before and after training. There will always be a physio available at the training ground if I want to see one. That’s not typical.’

Klarer and fellow defender Phil Neumann have not missed a game through injury as Blues players since joining in 2024 and 2025 respectively.

There have been subtle changes, though. Many of the logos and messages from TBRx – Brady’s performance and fitness company – have disappeared from the walls of the training ground in rural Warwickshire. They will be replaced by branding for the recently-launched ‘Keep Right On’ initiative as well as messages that boss Chris Davies believes are particularly relevant to his squad.

At this stage, certainly not. Knighthead remain determined to push forward their vision for Blues, with the £2billion Sports Quarter project at its heart.

The centrepiece of the Sports Quarter is the Powerhouse – a 62,000-seat stadium development that Blues hope will be one of the best in the country.

Blues may have lost their most famous face but all indications are that Brady’s departure is not a sign of Knighthead scaling back their commitment. The US group still believe Birmingham can become one of England’s most prominent clubs and are hugely excited by their progress this term, with Davies’ men top of the Championship heading into the November international break.

Knighthead still believe Birmingham can become one of England’s most prominent clubs and are hugely excited by their progress this term

Chris Davies’ men are top of the Championship heading into the November international break

It is easy to categorise Brady as a mere figurehead but that would be unfair. The 2025 Amazon Prime docuseries Built In Birmingham: Brady & The Blues was streamed in about 200 countries. There is no doubt that Brady’s presence helped Blues push certain transfer deals over the line, with Brady conducting video calls with targets. Earlier this season, Davies was late for a press conference because he had been on the phone to Brady.

The 49-year-old had a good relationship with the squad, too. He developed a strong rapport with former Blues forward Alfie May and even appeared on a FaceTime call during the wedding of May’s brother.

Equally, it would be unwise to exaggerate Brady’s role. If Blues win promotion this term, it will be a combination of Knighthead’s investment and the work of Davies and his players. By elevating the club’s profile globally, perhaps Brady has already done his job. Now it is time for the class of 2026 to write their own story.

During the early part of Brady’s time at St Andrew’s, the club leaned heavily into their rivalry with Wrexham, who are owned by Hollywood star Ryan Reynolds and his fellow actor Rob McElhenney.

When Blues took on Wrexham in September 2024, their 3-1 win was almost a sideshow. As well as the three famous Americans, David Beckham was also at St Andrew’s. When the clubs met, the US stars traded friendly insults before and after the match, generating a great deal of attention on social media.

David Beckham (right) was among the famous faces to take in a Birmingham game alongside Brady

Knighthead remain determined to push forward their vision for Blues, with the £2billion Sports Quarter project at its heart. The centrepiece is the Powerhouse – a 62,000-seat stadium

There was less of this when Blues won 2-1 at Wrexham earlier this season and perhaps that was no coincidence. There have certainly been those at Blues who feel that, at times, the club bought into the Wrexham rivalry a little too much and that forging their own path might be more fruitful.

There is no suggestion that Brady pushed the links with Wrexham yet if he is no longer associated with Blues, they may decline naturally.

In Brady’s first season, Blues were relegated to League One, with the NFL star admitting the club had tried to change too much, too soon. The appointment of Wayne Rooney was the highest-profile of those errors.

Brady departs with the club as healthy as it has been for some time. Even if he was rarely central to that recovery, he deserves at least some of the credit for it.

The Republic of Ireland will look to close the gap to the top of their Nations League B group by beating hosts Austria on Saturday at Raiffeisen Arena.

The hosts have taken four points form Kosovo, who they drew 1-1 with on October 4 in their most recent outing in the group stage.

Das Team are unbeaten in their past four games in all competitions, scoring nine goals in that time, though they have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their eight most recent matches.

Austria are in fact undefeated in their last 14 fixtures when designated as hosts, getting the better of opponents on 11 occasions.

Ireland have never been in League A of the Nations League, though they cannot afford to take a potential promotion charge for granted given last-placed Israel are only three points behind in the relegation spot.

The Boys in Green were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Israel on October 4, though the Irish did not have the benefit of playing at home after the clash was moved to a neutral venue.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson will be immensely disappointed that his side lost 1-0 against Kosovo on September 24 as it represents his team's only defeat in eight games, though a victory on the weekend would be just their second win in six matches.

The visitors' recent record against their hosts has been positive considering they are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Austria, winning once in that time.

A success for Ireland would be their second consecutive triumph when playing away from home, but a defeat would be their fifth in nine games.

Midfielder Nicolas Seiwald is in line to make his 56th appearance for the national team, while Xaver Schlager could earn a 60th cap.

Marco Grull has pulled out of the squad due to injury, while Patrick Wimmer has not been selected, so expect to see Raul Florucz on the right side of attack.

Ireland will have every chance of playing well as long as Caoimhin Kelleher is protecting their goal, with Troy Parrott stationed up front.

In the middle of the pitch, Finn Azaz and Conor Coventry could be paired together, while John Egan is likely lead his nation's defence.

A Schlager; Posch, Bacher, Danso, Laimer; Seiwald, X Schlager; Florucz, Schmid, Prass; Gregoritsch

Ireland have been poor away from home, though they boast a positive record against their opponents.

Austria's performances at home have been excellent, but while they are unlikely to lose, they may have to settle for just a point.

#1723. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1722. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

The newspaper reported that the Milan City Council had approved a bipartisan measure to halt the current environmental assessment process for the Generali Stadium project and request a new one that encompasses all the interventions the two clubs intend to undertake.

This includes the demolition of the current stadium once the new stadium is operational. The goal is to make the green light for the work conditional on a prior Health Impact Assessment (HIA).

MilanNews have learned that the City Council’s motion is non-binding, meaning Mayor Sala’s administration will not be obligated to follow the council’s request. More importantly, it does not suspend the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA).

The two clubs remain calm regarding the next phases, especially since the SEA and the VIS are two separate and distinct phases that must both be addressed before work on the new stadium can begin.

The Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a procedure established by Italian and European legislation that evaluates the environmental sustainability of a plan or program prior to its approval.

It differs from the subsequent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), which instead examines the environmental effects of a specific project prior to its potential authorisation and implementation.

The Council has therefore advanced a request that would not currently be foreseen under normal formal procedures. In any case, the two clubs are confident in the material produced, providing even more than necessary by integrating the Environmental Report with all the health-related details currently available.

Milan and Inter have no intention of avoiding any type of assessment. On the contrary, the EIA is scheduled for early 2027, by spring, with completion expected within a few months. Further investigations into the project and its impacts will therefore be undertaken shortly, as per the timetable.

Yesterday afternoon, Mayor Sala issues a statement on the news that broke, once again emphasising that the project will move forward.

“It’s clear that continuing to call the stadium issue into question is a gift to the right. I don’t want us to delude ourselves into thinking we’ve already won. I respect the City Council’s opinion, but the Council will respect the fact that I have no intention of reconsidering,” he said.

“We’ll discuss it in the City Council, but I have no intention of reconsidering the stadium. We’ve been talking about it for three years; everyone should do what they think best. I will continue to be consistent, and I will try to move forward with the stadium project.”

Councillor Martina Riva also gave a comment to MilanNews too: “Small obstacles? They won’t be a problem, we are convinced of the validity of our operation and we will move forward: the city, the teams and the fans who want a fully accessible stadium deserve it.

“I really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectationsaccessibleI really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectations.”

Jamaica will look to take control of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal when they welcome defending champions Mexico to the National Stadium in Kingston in the early hours of Sunday.

The Reggae Boyz finished second in League A Group B after two wins, a draw and a defeat in four group games, while the visitors entered at this stage as the top seed, but they arrive winless in four games under new head coach Rafael Marquez.

Jamaica secured their place in the last eight with a 1-1 draw away to Honduras, and have climbed two places to 69th in the latest FIFA rankings.

Interim head coach Rudolph Speid’s side opened the group with a 3-2 home win over Guatemala, with substitute Renaldo Cephas scoring in stoppage time.

They then lost 1-0 at home to 10-man Honduras, ending a 13-year winless run for the visitors against Jamaica, before Javon East’s brace sealed a 2-0 win at El Salvador, leaving the Reggae Boyz with six goals scored and four conceded in four group matches.

Speid is in the middle of a youth rebuild, and Jamaica have also lost two of their last four home games, while they have not won any of their last six meetings against Mexico (W4, D2), including a 1-0 win at the 2024 Copa America courtesy of Gerardo Arteaga’s 69th-minute goal.

Jamaica did hold Mexico to a 1-1 draw in Kingston in 2022 and led twice in a 2-2 draw at the Estadio Azteca in 2023.

Mexico have not looked like World Cup quarter-finalists since they were knocked out by England in the round of 16 and Javier Aguirre was replaced by Marquez.

The new boss’s first four games, all friendlies in the United States, brought 1-1 draws with Colombia and Peru before a 3-0 defeat to the USMNT and a 2-0 loss to Chile, scoring two goals and conceding seven across the four matches.

El Tri have also lost their last two away quarterfinals in this competition, though the head-to-head record in this fixture still heavily favours them, having won 21 of 29 previous meetings and lost only three.

There is plenty at stake, as the winners over two legs reach the 2027 Nations League Final Four and qualify automatically for the 2027 Gold Cup, while the losers drop into the Gold Cup preliminary round.

Jamaica have several important absentees, as Wrexham striker Bailey Cadamarteri has been left out so he can get minutes at club level, while QPR’s Rumarn Burrell and Coventry’s Ephron Mason-Clark are injured, the latter having hurt himself in training last Thursday.

Kaheem Parris is also out injured, while Leon Bailey, Ian Fray and Di’Shon Bernard missed out over match-fitness concerns, as all three have only recently returned from injury.

Ethan Pinnock also misses out, as Miguel Freckleton comes into the squad at left centre-half.

Andre Blake leads a 23-man squad that includes Damion Lowe, Joel Latibeaudiere, Javon East, Renaldo Cephas and Tyreece Campbell.

Mexico have called up 28 players, and Julian Quinones returns after scoring four goals at the World Cup, while Alexis Vega is also back after hinting at international retirement. ‘

Jesus “Tecatito” Corona returns for the first time since June 2022, and Osijek striker Armando Leon has his first senior call-up.

Raul Jimenez is out after knee surgery, while 18-year-old Gilberto Mora has recovered from the injury that forced him out of the last camp.

However, Speid’s side are missing several players and El Tri should have enough to edge the first leg and take a narrow advantage back to Monterrey.

#1717. The numbers suggest Chelsea are pushovers as they slide down the Premier League table... and club legend GUS POYET says it's time to prove they're up for a fight

Published: 07:38 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 10 November 2026

Morgan Rogers insisted it was no intentional drive-by. That he did not mean to knee Trai Hume in the head while the Sunderland defender was sitting up after a foul. Just an accident, honest.

The history shared between these two particular players opened the incident to interpretation.

Hume had folded Rogers like a deckchair in a 1-1 draw for Aston Villa last season. The challenge went viral. Sunderland shared it on their social media, glamourising it. Rogers responded at the time by saying: 'Great message to send out. Dangerous tackles getting highlight reels.'

At the Stadium of Light on Sunday, Hume was starting to sit up when Rogers caught him. Chelsea were losing 1-0, and frustrated. Their £117million arrival from Villa apologised immediately, so we will believe him when he says it was an innocent collision rather than retribution.

Nevertheless, Rogers does have an aggressive side to him. He squared up with Declan Rice at Arsenal, and James Tarkowski at Everton, and was signed in the summer partially for that passion.

Rogers has contested more duels than any other Chelsea player this season. He loses more than he wins, but is involved, for better or worse. He is Xabi Alonso's most-fouled footballer, while nobody has committed more fouls than this 6ft 2in England international.

Morgan Rogers (right) showed some fight during Chelsea's loss at Sunderland that appears to be lacking across the whole squad

If Rogers' team-mates showed the same mentality they may have avoided defeat on Sunday

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso needs his side to develop an aggressive streak

So when we ponder whether Alonso's Chelsea are pushovers, Rogers is arguably an exception. He is a hard nut surrounded by a soft shell, and that was a problem at Sunderland.

It was not only that Brian Brobbey bullied Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana. Regis Le Bris' side were all at it, a team of bouncers ready to rough up the lads planning to party. Cole Palmer and Co ended up getting tossed out of the Stadium of Light on their rears. Chelsea recorded 69 per cent possession - their highest of the Premier League season so far - but were second-best throughout.

Gus Poyet saw that. He played for Chelsea, managed Sunderland, and was an assistant to Dennis Wise at Leeds, who will be the next visitors to Stamford Bridge after this international break.

Daniel Farke's side have won more duels and aerial duels than any other Premier League team this season, which, given what we witnessed on Sunday, should be a concern for Alonso.

Poyet can predict what is coming. Chelsea-Leeds is already a fixture with a narrative attached. It never needs a second invitation to be talked up as 'dirty'. Alonso's side will need to show a willingness to compete if that awaits, more than they managed when travelling to Sunderland.

'Sunderland went to the game with that old-fashioned mentality,' the 58-year-old Uruguayan told Daily Mail Sport. 'Pressure from the fans, noise, tackling, "I'm gonna run over you". Chelsea went on to try to play. There was quite a big difference in that aggression. We see teams that are looking so much for an identity that they forget the process to win games.'

Poyet brought up Chelsea's 2-0 win at Everton last month. We told him how Alonso had admitted it was his favourite performance of the season, describing it as 'solid' and 'serious'.

'There you go,' said Poyet, who thinks before travelling to the Stadium of Light, it would have been worth showing Chelsea's players videos from that victory at the Hill Dickinson. It was a rare showing of seriousness from Alonso's side. Only David Moyes' Everton, with 83, have committed fewer fouls than Chelsea's 95 in the Premier League this season. While giving away free-kicks is hardly a cause for celebration, it is not the worst way of measuring whether you are there to push or be pushed.

Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey (left) bulled Chelsea's Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana (right)

'For me that was a proper old-fashioned game, being able to win like that,' Poyet said about Chelsea's win at Everton. 'Put the video on and say, "Play the same".

'Now I know what the other side are going to say after watching the Sunderland game. Leeds will be saying, 'Let's go'. Leeds are very solid, and very aggressive, so it can be that kind of game.

'More and more, through the years, I think from the pandemic to now, the difference between the teams is mental. Identity, positions, shapes, blah, blah, blah, but when they are right in here (in the head), it's big. Right now, Leeds, as a team, are a little ahead mentally.'

Alonso is a polite manager. Given the chance to have a pop at the refereeing at the Stadium of Light - how Chelsea were not awarded a penalty when Cole Palmer was sandwiched, but Sunderland were when Brobbey dropped down in front of Colwill - he declined. The Blues boss chose instead to decry his team's defending as substandard. Colwill was hooked at half-time, while there were two new summer signings in the back line in Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria who need to get to grips with the Premier League, sooner rather than later.

Poyet's first appearance after signing for Chelsea in 1997 was in the Charity Shield. Roy Keane welcomed him to English football with a kick to the head - with a little less subtlety than Rogers' knee on Hume. It finished 1-1 before Manchester United won on penalties.

Ex-Chelsea midfielder Gus Poyet has warned them of the threat Leeds pose later this month

Poyet learned a harsh lesson in that match, and not only from Keane's high kick. 'I couldn't get in the pace of the game,' Poyet recalls. 'I was always late. Ruud (Gullit) at half-time told me, "Gus, you're not really in the front, not really at the back". I said, "I'm trying!" The game was too fast.'

In a weird way, an ACL injury suffered by Poyet helped. He used the recovery time to prepare for returning. 'I went to the stadium, I was watching, learning the language, listening to Dennis Wise in the dressing room, getting that mentality,' he said. 'Then when I came back, I knew everything.

'That was my mentality. Some players need time. Some adjust quickly. You need to use all the time. For example, use this game against Sunderland when you play against Leeds. You cannot say, 'We didn't expect it'. Expect it! It's going to be similar.'

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

Liverpool and Aston Villa are reportedly monitoring highly rated Le Havre defender Djibril Ouziad, who could leave the Ligue 1 club next summer despite signing a long-term contract just two months ago.

The 17-year-old has emerged as one of the few bright spots in an otherwise disastrous campaign for the French side, establishing himself in the first team while Le Havre struggle at the bottom of the table.

According to Get French Football News, both Premier League clubs are keeping a close eye on Ouziad's development following his rapid breakthrough in France.

The report also suggests that the teenager is likely to leave Le Havre in the summer of 2027, regardless of whether the Normandy club manage to avoid relegation.

That prospect is particularly striking given that Ouziad only signed his first professional contract in September, committing his future to Le Havre until June 2030.

There is no indication that Liverpool or Aston Villa have submitted an offer, but the defender's emergence has already placed him on the radar of clubs competing in the Champions League.

Ouziad has made an immediate impression during his first season of senior football, featuring in nine Ligue 1 matches and starting eight of them.

Primarily deployed as a right wing-back, the French teenager is also capable of playing in a more conventional right-back role.

His performances have been particularly encouraging considering Le Havre's difficult circumstances.

The club have failed to win any of their opening 10 league matches, collecting just two points while suffering eight defeats.

That disastrous start resulted in the dismissal of Didier Digard, with former Crystal Palace and Blackburn Rovers defender Valerien Ismael appointed as his replacement.

Le Havre have also experienced significant upheaval behind the scenes, with president Jean-Michel Roussier and sporting director Demba Ba leaving the club following disagreements surrounding its management.

Despite that instability, Ouziad has continued to develop and has already been rewarded with international recognition.

The defender made his debut for France's Under-18 side earlier this season, further strengthening his reputation as an emerging talent.

His early progress has reportedly caught the attention of Liverpool and Aston Villa, although neither club is known to have opened formal negotiations.

For Liverpool, the link comes as the club continue assessing their defensive options under Andoni Iraola.

The Reds have previously explored reinforcements at right-back, having failed in a late attempt to sign Chelsea's Malo Gusto during the summer transfer window.

Ouziad would represent a considerably less experienced option, and there is no suggestion that Liverpool view him as an immediate solution to their first-team requirements.

Aston Villa's reported interest likewise remains at the monitoring stage, with the French youngster's development likely to be assessed over the coming months.

The most intriguing aspect of Ouziad's situation concerns the timing of a potential departure.

Le Havre secured the defender's first professional contract on September 1, tying him to the club until the summer of 2030.

Yet Get French Football News reports that a transfer at the end of the current campaign is already considered likely, regardless of the club's final position in Ligue 1.

The prediction does not mean Le Havre have decided to sell, nor does it establish that Ouziad is seeking an immediate move abroad.

However, his lengthy contract would give the French side considerable leverage should Liverpool, Aston Villa or another interested club decide to pursue a transfer.

Le Havre would not face the pressure of losing the teenager on a free transfer in the near future, potentially allowing them to demand a substantial fee for one of their most promising academy graduates.

No valuation has been reported, and it remains unclear what figure would persuade the Ligue 1 outfit to negotiate.

Liverpool already have experience of investing in emerging French defenders, having agreed a deal worth approximately £55m to sign Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes earlier this year.

The centre-back subsequently joined Iraola's squad for the 2026-27 season, demonstrating the club's willingness to invest in younger players with significant potential.

Ouziad is at a much earlier stage of his development, however, and his nine senior appearances provide only a limited indication of his long-term prospects.

For now, the teenager's immediate priority remains establishing himself in Le Havre's first team as the club attempts to recover from its miserable start to the season.

His future could nevertheless become an increasingly prominent transfer story if Liverpool or Aston Villa turn their reported interest into a concrete approach ahead of next summer.

#1710. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1709. Algeria vs Togo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 12 Nov 2026 21:57

Algeria host Togo at the Stade Hocine Ait Ahmed on Saturday, knowing that victory could strengthen their position at the top of Group I in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

The Desert Foxes lead the standings with four points from their opening two matches, one point ahead of the third-placed Sparrowhawks, who trail second-placed Zambia on goal difference, setting up an important double-header between the two nations.

Algeria have made a solid start under Brahim Hemdani, who remains unbeaten in his three matches in charge since September following Vladimir Petkovic's departure in August.

Petkovic's final game at the helm was a defeat to Switzerland in the World Cup round of 32, but Hemdani has since overseen a 3-1 victory over Zambia in the opening fixture of the AFCON qualifiers before his side recovered from two goals down to earn a 2-2 draw at Burundi on matchday two.

Algeria have now scored at least twice in three consecutive matches, including a 2-1 friendly victory over Niger in Tizi Ouzou in October, when Mohamed Belloumi and Ramy Bensebaini turned the game around after the North Africans conceded in the first half.

While that result extended the Desert Foxes’ impressive run, it also highlighted their recent defensive problems, having conceded 13 goals in their last seven matches across all competitions without keeping a clean sheet.

However, the hosts have kept Togo at bay in four of their last five meetings and won six of the most recent seven encounters between the sides across friendlies and competitive matches, which should give them confidence heading into Saturday's contest.

Togo are bidding to reach the AFCON finals for the first time since 2017 and made a winning start to their qualifying campaign by beating Burundi 1-0 in Lome, thanks to a goal from Dermane Karim.

However, Patrice Neveu's side failed to build on that success, suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Zambia on matchday two, which brought their six-match unbeaten run across all competitions to an end.

The defeat also marked the first time Togo had failed to score in six outings this year, since their goalless draw against South Africa in October 2025 during the final round of the World Cup qualifiers, where they finished fourth in Group B.

Currently 120th in the FIFA World Rankings, Les Eperviers face a difficult task against an Algeria side ranked 92 places higher, with Saturday's encounter also marking the first leg of a demanding double-header before the teams meet again in Lome three days later.

Togo also have a poor away record to overcome heading into this weekend’s clash, having managed just one victory in their last 13 matches outside their home country (D6, L6), dating back to a 2-1 friendly win over Niger in March 2024.

#1708. GdS: Milan open to Camarda loan to aid development – move abroad also possible

AC Milan’s plan to strengthen the attack in January could have a knock-on impact on Francesco Camarda’s fate, a report claims.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport makes the bold claim that Milan are readying a winter attempt for Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge. His price tag is already €50m, but the idea is to invest in the young striker and potentially pair him with Goncalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tresoldi’s fate intersects with that of Camarda. The Milan academy graduate has barely exceeded 100 minutes of playing time this season, 119 to be precise: 83 in the Europa League, with a single start against Salzburg, and another 36 in Serie A.

He hasn’t scored and had only one real chance to score, against Bologna. He needs to play to showcase his qualities, so the club believe it’s best to try do this elsewhere, before returning fit and ready to play for the Rossoneri.

The new development is that Camarda could develop at another Serie A team, or potentially return further enriched by experience abroad. There’s no shortage of options outside of Italy, but it will be a dry loan with no option to make it permanent.

Having arrived as a child in the Milan youth academy, he won an U15 Scudetto. He also achieved a historic record: with a federal exemption required because he was still a teenager, Camarda made his Serie A debut for AC Milan on 25 November 2023, late in the match against Fiorentina.

On that occasion, he became the youngest debutant in Serie A history (15 years, 8 months, and 15 days) and the youngest debutant in Milan’s history, surpassing the previous record set by Paolo Maldini, who made his debut at 16 years, 6 months, and 25 days.

In 2024, he signed his first professional contract and began his experience with Milan Futuro, the club’s second team, created specifically to nurture Milan’s talents, without necessarily having the need to send them elsewhere to develop.

That same season, at 16 years and 226 days, he became the youngest Italian player ever to make his Champions League debut. In 2025-26, it was time to try Serie A, where he could consistently play: he moved to Lecce, where, in 23 appearances, he scored his first (and so far only) league goal.

He was bought by the Giallorossi, and then bought back by Milan (who reserved a buy-back clause), with a contract extended until the summer of 2031 in the summer, plus an option for another year.

After progressing through Italy’s youth teams, Camarda truly found his calling with the U21s, scoring four goals in six games. He was also called up to the senior national team, playing for Baldini’s ‘experimental’ squad, making two appearances.

#1707. Wigan Athletic vs Barnsley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 12 Nov 2026 22:20, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 18:36

Two of the bottom four teams in the League One table will meet in an important contest at the Brick Community Stadium on Saturday, as Wigan Athletic welcome Barnsley.

The hosts have climbed off the foot of the division with a win and a draw in their last two games, while their visitors now sit 23rd and two points worse off.

Wigan Athletic return to action at the Brick Community Stadium aiming to continue an improvement in League One and a four-match unbeaten streak in all competitions.

They endured a dismal start to the 2026-27 season, picking up just seven points from their first 12 games having won just two and lost nine of those while scoring just eight goals and conceding 20.

That culminated in three straight defeats for the Latics in late October, falling to Oxford United, Huddersfield Town and Leicester City in three straight away games, before making a crucial return to winning ways at home to fellow strugglers Bromley with Christian Saydee, K'Marni Miller and Bradley Burrowes scoring in a hard-fought 3-2 triumph.

A goalless stalemate with Mansfield Town followed, before Gary Caldwell's side headed into consecutive cup games, beating Boreham Wood 3-0 away from home in the FA Cup last weekend and Crewe Alexandra 2-1 in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday with Jeremiah Chilokoa-Mullen and Rimmer Harrison scoring in the latter.

Now with some renewed confidence and their longest unbeaten streak since April, having moved within a point of escaping the bottom four while winning two and drawing one of their last three home league games, Wigan Athletic will look for another three-point haul on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, will hope to leapfrog their hosts on the back of a pair of cup wins of their own.

Back under the management of Daniel Stendel following a change over the summer, Barnsley have endured a similarly poor start to the League One season, now sitting ninth after 12 games with just nine points on the board, having managed two wins alongside seven defeats.

In those 12 outings, the Reds have conceded 22 goals and are winless in their last eight matches in the league, most recently hosting Oxford United on the back of four straight defeats and drawing 1-1, despite being reduced to 10 men inside 10 minutes, as they then led through Vimal Yoganathan and were pegged back.

A break in third-tier action then came in the FA Cup and EFL Trophy, firstly thrashing Aldershot 7-2 to advance in the former before beating Oldham Athletic 5-2 on Wednesday with Makenzie Kirk scoring a brace alongside goals from Daniel Johnson, Yoganathan and Luke Alker.

Having rebuilt crucial optimism with a pair of convincing cup wins, on the back of an improved display against Oxford, Barnsley will now bid to make it three straight wins and a first league victory since early September to boost their own standing at the bottom end of the table.

Wigan Athletic will likely be without forward Scott Hogan, who picked up an injury against Mansfield and missed their two cup games, while Dara Costelloe and Luke Harris should also miss out.

Those absences leave the Latics light up top, and Reggie Walsh and Bradley Burrowes may support lone front man Christian Saydee.

Fraser Murray started in both cup games having returned from a suspension off the bench against Mansfield and could start at the weekend, while Charlie Gray and Jon Mellish will likely compete to join Max Power in midfield.

Barnsley remain without defender Connor O'Riordan and attackers Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo through injury.

Key midfielder Patrick Kelly is also away on international duty with Northern Ireland, meaning Daniel Johnson should partner Luca Connell in the engine room after his midweek goal.

Ahead of them, Makenzie Kirk, who got a brace on Tuesday, should get the nod to lead the line with support from Yoganathan, Cameron McGeehan and Reyes Cleary.

For that reason, we can envisage the contest ending level at the Brick Community Stadium as both push to continue unbeaten streaks.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Our 125 anniversary & one of the best days! 💫 pic.twitter.com/YbZLTFPpWN

I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season.

Pascal Gross pulling the strings. 🔎 @Microsoft pic.twitter.com/DAgVsG2B3W

Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions in three consecutive seasons.

Like Everton, Newcastle labour to a home win which should have been more comfortable. It would have been had Wissa scored his penalty, but it was a nervy finish as Hull pushed for an equaliser after Cho’s goal.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

One of the outstanding team performances of the season so far from Brighton, and it will take some beating between now and May. Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

Kai Havertz shoots straight at the goalkeeper when clean through, and that is surely Arsenal’s last chance of an unlikely comeback gone. Brighton have pushed Arsenal back for much of the season half, they have not been sitting on a lead.

At St James’ Park, Hull have pulled a goal back through Cho to set up a nervy finish for Newcastle.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

What a farcical five minutes we have had, from an absurd disallowed goal for Everton to a ridiculous red card for Abdul Fatawu, banished for a second bookable offence - which was diving. There is going to be plenty said about Thierno Barry’s second goal being chalked out because, when you see it, you will wonder what it was for. These are the situations with which I struggle most - if players do not appeal for a wrongdoing, if they don’t feel they have been the victims of an injustice, why are officials getting involved?

Thierno Barry thought he had made it two for Everton, but the goal has been ruled out because Brennan Johnson was judged to be interfering with play and offside. You’re never getting those this weekend after the Enzo Fernandez incident.
